content: Sister Frances Dominica Ritchie, FRC, is a British nurse who has dedicated her career to specializing in palliative care. From a very young age, Sister Frances was deeply influenced by her religious upbringing in Edinburgh, where her grandfather served as an elder in the Church of Scotland. Despite this religious environment, her aspiration to become a nurse began at the age of three. Her early experiences in caregiving were shaped by her younger brother, David Ritchie, who was born with only one lung and was five-and-a-half years her junior. As a child, she frequently visited her brother at Great Ormond Street Hospital, which further solidified her desire to pursue nursing. She later attended the prestigious Cheltenham Ladies' College. Sister Frances chose to specialize in palliative care after a profound encounter with a two-year-old girl named Helen, who had undergone surgery for a cerebral tumor and was left in a comatose state. Recognizing the immense burden on Helen's parents, Sister Frances began taking the child into her own home periodically to provide the family with much-needed respite. This experience inspired her to establish Helen House in Oxford, the first-ever hospice dedicated to children. Helen House became a pioneering institution in pediatric palliative care, and Sister Frances continues to serve as a trustee. In January 2007, the hospice was featured in a BBC2 documentary series titled The Children of Helen House. Building on the success of Helen House, Sister Frances later founded Douglas House, a facility designed to provide care for individuals aged 16 to 40 who are living with life-limiting conditions. Opened in 2004 by Her Majesty The Queen, Douglas House is located on the same grounds as Helen House. Both facilities offer a range of services, including respite care (with the option for family members to stay), end-of-life care, and ongoing family support. This support extends from the time of referral and continues for as long as the family desires, even years after the death of their loved one. Sister Frances has also made notable media appearances, including as a guest on BBC Radio 4's Desert Island Discs.
